intake.omit_after: An attractive text box may conceal

sections.label: Ranking methods
sections.applicability: Include when discussing rank fusion, learning to rank or reranking. Mark individual methods not used by this product as Not applicable and record the reason.

sections.label: Generated answers (RAG)
sections.applicability: Include when the product generates answers from retrieved material. Record the specific answer-generating mode being reviewed.

questions.listen_for: what is recognised, what is rewritten or added, and whether each change can be seen and exported. “Our AI understands your question” describes none of them.
who picks the next step (a fixed sequence, a choice among named branches, or a model’s plan) and the limits on tools, sources and rounds. “Agentic” on its own does not answer this.
the components, the order they run in and the number of candidates kept at each cut-off. “Hybrid” or “semantic” without numbers is a label, not an answer.
a job for each named model: parsing, first-stage retrieval, sparse expansion, reranking or writing. “Powered by BERT” names a model, not a stage.
the unit at each stage: what is indexed for retrieval and what is passed on later. “We search full text” should say at which stage.
one stated rule (combined, best passage only, or shown separately) and whether several passages from one paper can crowd out other papers.
where the lists meet, the combining rule and the depth of each list. Two modes demonstrated side by side do not show how they are combined.
a way to switch expansion off, or a mode that matches the string exactly, demonstrated on your own identifiers rather than described.
concrete treatment of case, hyphens and identifiers on the lexical path, and a test of new or unusual strings on the dense path. “The model handles any vocabulary” is not a test.
failure cases the vendor has tested, including ones that went wrong. A demonstration made only of successful paraphrases does not answer this.
the kinds of training data and how the model was adapted to scholarly material. “Trained on millions of papers” says what it read, not what it was taught to rank.
whether the explanation records what actually ran or is written afterwards. A fluent “why this result” paragraph may be the second.
a list of what an export actually contains, and whether a rerun reuses the saved query or generates a new one.
a change log or version identifier that can be tied to a saved search. “We continuously improve the model” means results can change without notice.
prices and limits in numbers, and what the user sees when a limit is reached. A search that silently becomes shallower is the answer to watch for.

questions.omit_after: Chapter 12 records both kinds of change:
questions.listen_for: a notice period and an export route that covers stored traces as well as saved searches.
evaluation on queries like yours, with results broken down by query type. A single benchmark average or leaderboard rank does not answer this.
willingness to run searches your library already knows are difficult. A vendor that offers only its own demonstration queries has not answered.
a way to rerun a saved query set after an update and compare the results. If the only record is a release note, regressions will go unseen.
the contributing lists, their depths and any weights. “We use RRF” on its own leaves every part of this open.
the features, where the labels came from and when the model was last retrained. Click labels without bias correction reward whatever was already shown first.
candidate counts at each stage and what text each stage saw. A reranker cannot recover what the first stage did not return.
metrics at a stated cut-off, measured on this collection and task, with the queries that got worse. An average gain can hide them.
a named retriever for this mode, and whether the choice changes from query to query.
two answers, not one: the indexed unit and the unit the model reads. They are often different.
a rewritten query you can see and export, not only a description of the rewriting.
a number, and the rule that chose those items from the candidate set.
fixed steps or model-chosen actions, with the limits on rounds and tools.
two separate evaluations. A faithfulness score says nothing about what retrieval missed.
a trace of what reached the model’s input. Without one, a missing citation cannot be located.
